### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via sharing_rule (literal, a string literal in SysMetadataActivation; a string literal in a comment in ISharingRuleService))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via sharing_rule (literal, a string literal in SysMetadataActivation; a string literal in a comment in ISharingRuleService))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/sharing-service.mdx`  _(via ISharingRuleService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via declaredRuleNamed (symbol, a method of interface DeclaredSharingRuleReader; a method of interface ISharingRuleService), declaredRuleNamed (literal, a string literal in DeclaredSharingRuleReader), sharing_rule (literal, a string literal in SysMetadataActivation; a string literal in a comment in ISharingRuleService), /security/_activation/sharing_rule/:name (route, a path literal in a comment in ISharingRuleService))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via sharing_rule (literal, a string literal in SysMetadataActivation; a string literal in a comment in ISharingRuleService))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **149** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 80ec71dc26036d43bac03186224fc673864da517` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5b966f9da026f1e7a61fb3e88688102c43c691ff` — the merge of head `672daf099fdc51d6fb44c2bcb3c9b907f4370329` into base `80ec71dc26036d43bac03186224fc673864da517`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5b966f9da026f1e7a61fb3e88688102c43c691ff && git checkout 5b966f9da026f1e7a61fb3e88688102c43c691ff
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 80ec71dc26036d43bac03186224fc673864da517 672daf099fdc51d6fb44c2bcb3c9b907f4370329 && git checkout -B drift-repro 80ec71dc26036d43bac03186224fc673864da517 && git merge --no-ff 672daf099fdc51d6fb44c2bcb3c9b907f4370329

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 80ec71dc26036d43bac03186224fc673864da517
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 80ec71dc26036d43bac03186224fc673864da517` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `672daf099fdc51d6fb44c2bcb3c9b907f4370329`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/catalog-activation.ts, content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx, packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-metadata-activation.object.ts, .changeset/25187-declared-rule-reader-contract.md, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/declared-sharing-rules.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/activation-gate.ts, packages/core/src/utils/metadata-activation-store.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/rest/src/sharing-routes.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/security/tenancy-posture.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-activation-store.ts, packages/objectql/src/action-activation.ts, content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx, docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md, docs/adr/0126-packaged-metadata-customization-model.md

Reviewed 2026-10-22T16:17Z on card #25187 (body and all four comments, the `os-dev-report` 6344788817 included), PR #25250 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at `f2ade4afb`), and the 39 check-runs on the head. Every path of the diff is inside this scope, so there is no TIER_DEFAULT remainder for the lane seat. The head did not move during the review.

**Check-runs on the head (the gate verdicts).** All 39 completed: 0 failure, the rest success or skipped (opt-in and matrix-skipped lanes). Green by name: Check Changeset, Lint (ESLint, docs & code guards, repo & tooling gates, CI/release/engine gates, PM dispatch-gates, scoped lanes), Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Test Core 1–6, Build Core, Build Docs, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, the card/branch claim guards, Dogfood Regression Gate. At the first read 15 of these were still in progress; by this write all had concluded.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`ISharingRuleService.declaredRuleNamed?(name)` — a widening, right.** An optional method on a published interface: every existing implementer still satisfies the contract without change, and a caller must narrow before calling. The one in-tree implementer, `SharingRuleService` (`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts:1050`), returns `Promise<DeclaredSharingRule | null>`; `DeclaredSharingRule` (`declared-sharing-rules.ts:144`) carries `name: string` and `packageId?: string`, so it is structurally assignable to the declared `{ name: string; packageId?: string } | null`. The dev's reverse verification (return mutated to `name: number`, tsc red at `catalog-activation.ts(159,36)` and `sharing-rule-service.ts(1050,9)` TS2416) is consistent with that reading: the contract now binds both consumers. The docblock's claims (answers for the declaration in every organization, ledger-independent; the door records `packageId`; optional, caller probes and refuses fail-closed with 503) each match the code read below. Right.
2. **The runtime door's switch from its local duck type to the contract type keeps the 503-when-absent behaviour — right.** `type DeclaredSharingRuleReader = Required<Pick<ISharingRuleService, 'declaredRuleNamed'>>` (`catalog-activation.ts:120`) is the same shape the deleted local interface spelled. `declaredSharingRuleReaderOf` still probes `typeof candidate?.declaredRuleNamed === 'function'` (line 124); `DECLARATION_LOOKUPS.sharing_rule.lookup` still returns `undefined` when the probe fails (line 159); the `!pending` arm still answers `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, a rejected read 503, a `null` answer 404 (lines 287–325). No control flow moved. The alias is module-local and the import is `import type`, so nothing new reaches runtime's public surface; the dev's dist grep (0 files for the alias, the contract name and the new comment; the positive control `declaredSharingRuleReaderOf` in 2 files) is consistent with that. Right.
3. **The ledger's `metadata_type` description — right, and complete at this head.** Every writer of `sys_metadata_activation` on this head: `flow` (`service-automation/src/flow-activation-store.ts`, extends `ObjectStoreMetadataActivationStore`), `action` (`objectql/src/action-activation.ts`, same), and `position` / `permission` / `sharing_rule` / `webhook` (`catalog-activation.ts:396`, `CATALOG_ACTIVATION_SUBJECTS`). The other `metadata_type` references in `core`, `plugin-auth` and `plugin-sharing` are readers of `position` / `permission`. The six names listed are the six written. A `description` on a system object's field is not something a metadata author writes, so it moves no authorable surface. Right.
4. **The docs paragraph in `sharing-rules.mdx`, claim by claim against the cited code — every claim holds.**
   - *Read-only: `DELETE …/sharing/rules/:idOrName` on a declared name answers `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, switched off or not.* `SharingRuleService.deleteRule` (line 1158): no row found, then `declaredRuleNamed(idOrName)` truthy, then it throws an `Error` whose message starts `PERMISSION_DENIED:`; `declaredRuleNamed` reads the declared source without consulting the ledger, so a switched-off rule still answers. The REST prefix arm (`packages/rest/src/sharing-routes.ts:578`, and the `['PERMISSION_DENIED', 403]` map at line 386) renders it as 403 with `code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED'`. Right. (The PR body cites this file as `sharing-routes.ts handleError`; it lives in `packages/rest`, not in plugin-sharing. The mdx itself cites only the service, so nothing in the published text is wrong.)
   - *`PUT …/meta/sharing_rule/:name` is refused too.* `sharing_rule` is a registry type in `metadata-plugin.zod.ts:190` under the `allowRuntimeCreate: false` ruling; `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx:121` (unchanged, linked from the new section) spells the answer, `403 NOT_CREATABLE` / `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`. Consistent.
   - *The door writes one `sys_metadata_activation` row (`metadata_type: 'sharing_rule'`, no organization column), the same request revokes or re-derives the grants.* `ObjectStoreMetadataActivationStore.setActive` (`core/src/utils/metadata-activation-store.ts:260`) writes exactly one row keyed by `(metadata_type, name)`; `bindSharingRuleActivationReconcile` (`sharing-rule-service.ts:325`) registers `afterInsert` / `afterUpdate` / `afterDelete` on `METADATA_ACTIVATION_TABLE` and calls `reconcileDeclaredRuleActivation(name)`, which purges `{ source: 'rule', source_id: name }` when the rule is served nowhere and runs `evaluateResolvedRule` per projection when it is (lines 1068–1078). Right.
   - *The door confirms the name through `declaredRuleNamed`; unknown name 404; no reader 503.* Item 2 above. Right.
   - *A new row under a declared name is refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, so is a rename onto one; applies to `POST …/sharing/rules`, Setup's forms, scripts and imports through the data API; an update that keeps its name is not affected.* `DeclaredSharingRuleNameConflictError` declares `code = 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT'`, `status = 409` (lines 251–253); `defineRule`'s create branch throws it (line 834); `bindDeclaredRuleNameGuard` registers `beforeInsert` and `beforeUpdate` on `sys_sharing_rule` (lines 308–309), and the update arm returns early when `data.name === previous.name` (line 301). The message names the clone path. System writes pass (line 293), which the docs do not contradict. Right.
   - *Who may flip: `manage_metadata` (403), then under `group` / `isolated` the platform operator, the message naming the operator; under `single` the `manage_metadata` holder is enough.* `refuseUngrantedActivationAuthoring` requires `ACTIVATION_AUTHORING_CAPABILITY = 'manage_metadata'` and answers `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`; `refuseUngrantedActivationWrite` returns `undefined` when no posture or `!postureEnforcesWall(posture)` (`tenancy-posture.ts:53`: wall = `posture !== 'single'`), else requires `ec.posture === 'PLATFORM_ADMIN'`, else 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` with `SHARING_RULE_ACTIVATION_SUBJECT.remedy`, which reads "ask your platform operator". Right.
   - *The reconcile-failure window: the hook runs after the row is written, no transaction wraps the two; a throw reaches the door, which answers the error instead of 200; the row keeps its new value; boot heals; the same switch again re-runs the reconcile.* `ObjectQL.opensAfterAbortUnit` (`engine.ts:5522`) opens a unit only for a hook entry with `meta` (a metadata-bound hook); the reconcile handler is registered through plain `registerHook` with `object` / `packageId` / `priority` and no `meta`, so no unit is opened; `setActive` opens no transaction of its own; `triggerHooks` (`engine.ts:5443`) awaits each handler with no catch, so the throw leaves `engine.update`, and the door's catch answers `deps.errorFromThrown(err, 503)` (`catalog-activation.ts:409`). At boot, `kernel:bootstrapped` (`sharing-plugin.ts:1074`) runs `backfillRuleGrants` over `listRules({})`, then `sweepOrphanedRuleGrants`; `declaredRules` filters out `readSwitchedOffDeclaredRules()` (line 943), so a switched-off declaration has no live projection and its name-keyed grants are revoked by the sweep (lines 1272–1335), and a switched-on one is re-derived by the backfill. A repeat switch always issues an `update` when the row exists (`setActive`, line 270), and `afterUpdate` fires on it. Right. One edge the docs leave out and need not state: under unknown declared scopes (`declaredScopes === null`) the sweep holds every declared name live and revokes nothing (line 1296); that is the service's deliberate fail-safe, not a counter-claim.
   - The section's placement (inside "Criteria-Based Sharing Rules", after "Switching a rule off withdraws the access it granted", before "There is no share every record rule") and its `{basePath}` spelling match the page's existing conventions. ADR-0131 D6's `sharing_rule` note (read-only, clonable, same-name shadowing retired, deployment-level and operator-gated under a wall) is what the section paraphrases.
5. **No accept-set change anywhere else.** `plugin-sharing` is untouched; no Zod schema, registry row, route or error code moves; no generated artifact in the tree carries the changed strings (`git grep` at the head: `declaredRuleNamed` appears only in the five diff files and the door's test; the old description string survives only in ADR-0126:205, which is ③ item 1). Spec's `check:generated` ("All 14 generated artifacts are up to date") and the green Spec property liveness and Lint lanes agree.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and in the changeset body, both line-initial — **true**: one optional member added to a published contract, every implementer still compiles, every caller still compiles.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` — **true**: nothing a metadata author can write changes (a contract method and a system field's description are not authorable keys, values or types).
- `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/platform-objects` at `patch` — **right** for a non-protocol widening (AGENTS.md § Post-Task Checklist step 3: `none` takes `patch`). Not `skip-changeset`, correctly: two released packages publish.
- `@objectstack/runtime` not listed — **acceptable**: the runtime change is a module-local type alias plus an `import type`, and emits nothing to `dist` (the dev's measure, consistent with the source read). Independently, `.changeset/config.json` places `@objectstack/runtime` in the same `fixed` group as `@objectstack/spec`, so it versions in lockstep with the two listed packages whatever the changeset names. Check Changeset is green on the head.
- No `major`, no BREAKING banner, no ADR-0087 disposition owed: nothing is removed, renamed or tightened.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none declared by the dev; none found here.
- **Deviation — branch `claude/project-thread-7afd2e` instead of `claude/issue-25187-*`.** The newest Claim on the card (6343530887) names this branch and the seat's platform exception; the gate "The card this PR closes must claim this branch" is green. Answered: no action.
- **Deviation — `packages/runtime/src/domains/catalog-activation.ts` touched beyond the claim's three files.** Type-only, stated in the PR body, and the dispatch asked for the door to read the contract type in the same PR. It is inside this record's scope (item ① 2) and judged there. Answered: no action.
- **Deviation — PR body opens with the attribution HTML comment, `Fixes #25187` on line 4.** A dispatch instruction the dev followed; the claim guards are green, and it is not a contract matter. Answered: no action.
- **Deviation — `origin/main` not merged, 5 commits behind.** None of the five touches these packages or files; CI judged the merge ref and every lane is green. Answered: no action.
- **Out-of-scope finding 1 — ADR-0126:205 still lists `metadata_type` as `('flow', 'permission', …)`.** Confirmed on the head. The table row is illustrative (ellipsis) rather than wrong, and ADR-0126 is a governed surface (Tier H), so it cannot ride this PR. Answer: **card** — a p4 docs-only card for a maintainer-worded ADR touch-up, dedupe words "ADR-0126 metadata_type column list sharing_rule webhook". Not a maintainer escalation: nothing is blocked by it.
- **Out-of-scope finding 2 — no end-to-end HTTP pin for the `/data` door answering 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` from `bindDeclaredRuleNameGuard`.** The envelope is pinned at the class (`code` / `status`) and in `sharing-rule.test.ts`; the transport reads thrown `status` / `code` through its shared rule. A socket-level pin is a test-only addition the `domain:spec`-adjacent lane can take when it next touches the door. Answer: **card** — a p4 test-only card to the plugin-sharing/runtime lane; not a defect, not a maintainer matter.
